Other actions (weak nose wrinkle, moderate upper-lip raise) can co-occur with intense smiling due to cheek compression but do not override the dominant positive valence. Normal voice parameters provide no conflicting cues.

Downturned mouth corners are a weaker/secondary element that does not override the dominant markers.

Other elements (quiet loudness, downward gaze, raised chin) are secondary and do not override the core smile indicators or match any alternative emotion (e.g., contempt would typically involve unilateral lip raise rather than bilateral stretch; confidence lacks the strong smile markers).

Higher pitch is a weaker match but can appear in variants of sadness involving strain; other emotions (fear typically has widened rather than tightened eyes and faster rate; confusion lacks the strong downward-gaze association; contempt usually pairs with more asymmetric facial cues not mentioned) fit the overall pattern less well.
